messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: elevated throttle events detected in prod/model-serving (service=model-serving-prod). 504 throttle events in last 5m, queue depth p95=78%, tokens/sec spike on shard-3. Paging on-call.
ryan_oncall: i'm on it. first: scope and customer impact?
ana: quick check — traffic spike from campaign-xyz? querying logs now.
ana: found increased concurrent streaming sessions from a single client IP range, but requests look valid (no retries). top model is rwd-vicuna-13b.
ryan_oncall: thanks. maria can you pull autoscaler and pod metrics? want current replicas + max, and any OOMs/restarts.
maria: helm query -> HPA target=cpu 60%, min=6 max=40 current=18. No OOMs, one restart on model-worker-3 2h ago.
kim: dashboard shows tokens/sec per-instance jumped 3x on shard-3. avg latency increased ~120ms at tail, 95th up ~600ms for long-sequence requests. client errors 5xx = no, 429s = yes (throttles).
ryan_oncall: mitigation plan: 1) temporarily raise HPA max to 60 and increase pod burst capacity 2) suppress noisy page alerts for queue-depth while we stabilize 3) enable canary route to dedicated pool for the heaviest customers 4) notify CS for impacted customers.
ana: running k scale set --replicas=36 deployment/model-worker-prod now (increase). will monitor for ~2m for queue drain.
maria: applied HPA override to max=60 and bumped concurrency limit on ingress to allow extra in-flight while autoscaler spins.
ana: queue depth dropped from 78% -> 52% in ~90s. throttle rate falling.
ryan_oncall: good. temporarily mute alert: /alerts mute alert:prod_model_queue_high for 15m (reason: active remediation, paging noise). leaving a pinned note.
monitoring-bot: action recorded: alert prod_model_queue_high muted by ryan_oncall for 15m.
kim: quick customer impact check: CS list shows three enterprise tenants with elevated tail latency (ids: corp-47, corpus-inc, bluewave). no API errors reported; degraded latency only. cs-olivia: on it, will notify account teams and prepare a message if SLA risk increases.
ana: logs show larger batches per request due to prefix caching growth — kv cache warm-up is accumulating for long session users. that increases tokens/sec for some workers.
ryan_oncall: follow-ups we must do after stabilization: - refine alerting: page only when throttle_events >= 300 AND sustained >= 3m, or queue_depth_p95 >= 90% AND tokens/sec_per_shard spikes. - add a dashboard panel for throttle_events_by_shard and tokens/sec normalized per-replica. - update runbook to include kv-cache growth as a cause and recommended mitigations (reduce per-request batch, isolate long-lived sessions).
maria: opening ticket INF-7452: "Autoscale + alert tuning: use tokens/sec + throttle events for paging, add shard panels, HPA recommended defaults" with checklist.
kim: proposed concrete thresholds in ticket: page when throttle_events_5m > 300 OR (queue_depth_p95 > 90 AND tokens/sec_p95_per_shard > baseline*2). for now set alert notification to page to p0 oncall only if both conditions met, otherwise channel notify.
ana: also suggest adding short debounce window (3m) to avoid single-minute spikes waking the pager.
ryan_oncall: agreed. assign to monitoring team. also recommend a small canary: route 5% of traffic for top customers to dedicated pool during peak windows to avoid customer impact.
cs-olivia: we'll reach out to corp-47 and bluewave to let them know we observed transient latency and steps taken. will report back if customers request formal incident.
monitoring-bot: created dashboard ticket DASH-2101 (owner: kim).
ryan_oncall: lessons: autoscaler reacts to CPU but workload cost is tokens/sec and KV cache growth; HPA alone isn't sufficient. we should evaluate a custom autoscaler that considers tokens/sec and throttle events.
nana: adding a quick snippet to reproduce tokens/sec query (use in ticket):
```
# tokens/sec per shard in last 5m
sum(rate(model_tokens_total{env="prod"}[5m])) by (shard)
```
and throttle events: 
```
sum(increase(model_throttle_events_total{env="prod"}[5m])) by (shard)
```
ryan_oncall: add to runbook: when throttles spike -> quick fixes = increase replicas, redirect heavy customers to dedicated pool, reduce batch size or concurrency, temporarily raise request timeouts; long term = autoscaler with tokens/sec and shard-aware routing.
maria: removing overrides now, HPA set back to max=40, replicas stabilizing at 22. queue depth at 48%, throttle events down to 12 in last 5m.
ryan_oncall: unmute alert earlier than scheduled.
monitoring-bot: alert prod_model_queue_high unmuted by ryan_oncall.
cs-olivia: informed account teams. no formal incident requested by customers at this time.
ryan_oncall: thanks all. creating post-incident checklist and will schedule a short retro with monitoring + serving runtime teams tomorrow to finalize thresholds and runbook changes. tagging owners: kim (dashboards), maria (autoscaler), ana (serving runtime), cs-olivia (customer comms).
maria: one follow-up note: consider adding a per-shard circuit-breaker to avoid single-shard storms taking down many workers.
kim: agreed. putting that in DASH-2101 and INF-7452.
ryan_oncall: closing thread for now — please update tickets with any additional findings. :thumbsup:
